evidence.positive: Against the running app at localhost:61175 (demo-demo), I built two cases via the admin API: case A = p-appendectomy (op 01a0353f-87fe-75a9-ba56-0ca9cca127ca, has pathways) and case B = p-hernia-repair (op 01a0353f-883b-7b18-bd1f-e82dc79b7295, zero pathways -> the 'prefers nothing' answer the old cache could not store). (1) EMPTY RESULT IS NOW CACHED: firing POST /api/admin/events/category-event (INDUCTION_START) on case B logged the recompute line 'Operation 01a0353f-883b-7b18-bd1f-e82dc79b7295 has no antibiotic pathways to walk under tenant TenantKey[value=demo-demo]: [p-hernia-repair drug=0 none=false] (tenant holds 64 pathways)' and Valkey then held hash key antibiotic-resolution-v2/tenant:demo-demo/op:01a0353f-883b-7b18-bd1f-e82dc79b7295 with field 01a0353c-8588-77f4-b051-bde6784a551a (= admin's user id) holding {"protocol":{"procedureProtocols":[],"noProphylaxisProcedures":[],"agreed":false},"preferred":[],"contraindicated":[]} and TTL 86382. Repeating the same event produced ZERO ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService log lines (grep count 0 over the log window) while EventService still logged 'Induction start time set' - i.e. the empty resolution was served from cache instead of re-resolving. (2) THE WHOLE RESOLUTION IS SERVED, not recomputed: for case A the stored value is the full protocol + preferred + contraindicated (preferred = step 1 CEFAZOLIN + METRONIDAZOLE). I overwrote that hash field with the same resolution but preferred swapped to its step-3 option, then called GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates: it returned ["step 3: VANCOMYCIN, LEVOFLOXACIN, and METRONIDAZOLE"] with 0 service log lines, where a genuine recompute returns ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE"] (I captured that baseline first). (3) KEY STAYS USER-SCOPED: scanning m-cefazolin via POST /api/cds/medication-selection as loopuser added a second field 01a0353c-85d7-72a4-aa7f-f3e5d5c90882 (= loopuser's user id) alongside admin's on the same case key, and loopuser's second scan produced 0 service log lines (its own hit).
evidence.negative: A superseded answer is NOT served. With case A cached and its hash field deliberately poisoned to the step-3 answer, I ran PATCH /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/classification {"classification":"EMERGENT"}. Valkey KEYS antibiotic* immediately afterwards listed only case B's key - case A's key was gone entirely. The next INDUCTION_START event on case A logged 'Finished ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.resolve - 28.32 ms' (a real recompute) and the freshly written entry held preferred = [{step:1, meds:[CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE]}], i.e. the poisoned step-3 answer was never handed back. I also confirmed a case-scoped write drops EVERY user's variant at once, which is the point of one key per case with a field per user: with both admin's and loopuser's fields present on case A, a single PATCH .../classification {"classification":"URGENT"} left EXISTS on the key = 0 and HKEYS empty. Separately, a legacy-shaped entry does not get served either: I SET the case key to a plain string (TYPE = string, i.e. the pre-OR-2726 storage shape), and the next GET .../antibiotic-candidates returned 200 [] rather than throwing, logged 'Discarding an unusable cached antibiotic resolution' with org.springframework.data.redis.RedisSystemException, and the key was dropped (TYPE = none, KEYS antibiotic* empty).
evidence.red_check: Two flips, both reverted. FLIP 1 (proves the positive's absence assertion is live): case B was serving from cache with 0 ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService log lines per event. I ran HDEL on its single hash field (HKEYS then returned empty) and fired the same INDUCTION_START event again - the recompute line came straight back: 'Operation 01a0353f-883b-7b18-bd1f-e82dc79b7295 has no antibiotic pathways to walk under tenant TenantKey[value=demo-demo]: [p-hernia-repair drug=0 none=false] (tenant holds 64 pathways)'. REVERTED: that recompute rewrote the entry ({"protocol":{...},"preferred":[],"contraindicated":[]} back at the same field), and the next event returned to 0 service lines and 0 warn lines. FLIP 2 (proves the fail-open guard the ticket asks for actually fires): I rewrote case A's cached JSON with protocol.agreed=false while leaving preferred non-empty, which violates AntibioticResolution's constructor Precondition. GET .../antibiotic-candidates then logged WARN 'Discarding an unusable cached antibiotic resolution' followed by 'com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.ValueInstantiationException: Cannot construct instance of `com.guided.orci.dto.AntibioticResolution`, problem: drugs can only be preferred on the authority of procedures that agree on a protocol' - and still returned 200 ["step 1: CEFAZOLIN and METRONIDAZOLE"], i.e. it recomputed instead of throwing on the alerting path. REVERTED: the poisoned entry was discarded by that read, and subsequent clean runs logged 0 occurrences of the warn while serving normal hits. I did not attempt the pre-fix class swap: the class was rewritten from ProcedureAntibioticCandidateRepository to AntibioticPathwayRepository by later tickets, so the parent-commit version does not compile against the shipped classpath.

red_check_signature: problem: drugs can only be preferred on the authority of procedures that agree on a protocol

automation.assessment: ProcedureAntibioticCandidateCacheTest covers four fail-open branches (unparseable entry, wrong Redis type, a write that throws, a repair delete that throws) and AntibioticResolutionSerializationTest covers round-tripping every Outcome plus forward-compatible binding of an older shape. All of the cache tests mock RedisService, so nothing exercises a real store-then-read round trip, and three things I validated by hand have no automated equivalent: that an empty resolution is stored and reused at all (the ticket's whole point), that one case-scoped invalidation drops every user's field, and that an entry which parses but trips AntibioticResolution's Preconditions is discarded rather than thrown. The last one matters because the existing 'stale entry' test feeds a bare UUID, which fails at the parser, not at the RuntimeException branch the ticket's fail-open bullet is written for. Worth adding as backend tests in orci/src/test; nothing here is worth a qa-suite e2e, since the cache is invisible through the UI except as latency.
proposed_tests: ProcedureAntibioticCandidateCacheTest: a case with no configured pathways caches its empty resolution and the second resolve is served from it (assert setHashValue body has preferred empty, then feed that body back to getHashValue and assert no second pathway walk).

ProcedureAntibioticCandidateCacheTest: a cached body with preferred non-empty and protocol.agreed=false is discarded and recomputed, covering the Preconditions RuntimeException branch rather than a parse failure.

ProcedureAntibioticCandidateCacheTest: invalidateCachedCandidates(operation) deletes the case key while invalidateCachedCandidates(operation, user) deletes only that user's field, so two users' cached answers are dropped together by a case-scoped change and independently by a user-scoped one.

OperationService/DefaultHL7ProcessingContext tests: a launch or scheduling message that moves a case's classification or procedure types deletes ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.cacheKeyForCase, and does so after commit rather than before.
An integration test that round-trips through a real Redis/Valkey rather than a mocked RedisService, so the hash storage shape and the 24h expiry on the case key are asserted end to end.

jira_comment:
Validated against a throwaway build of main (e7eeafd) on a disposable local stack. Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: on a demo case whose procedure configures no antibiotic pathways, the first resolve logged the recompute line and wrote the empty resolution into Valkey as a hash field under the case key, with a 24h TTL. Repeating the same event produced no ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService log lines at all - the answer that prefers nothing is now cached, which is the case that never cached before. I also confirmed the whole resolution is served, not just the ids: I edited the cached body of a second case to prefer its step-3 option and the antibiotic-candidates endpoint returned step 3 instead of the step 1 a recompute produces. A scan by a second user added its own field alongside the first on the same case key, so the answer stays user-scoped.

Negative: with that edited entry in place, patching the case classification deleted the case key outright, the next resolve recomputed, and the edited answer was never handed back. A single case-scoped change dropped both users' fields together. An entry left at the case key in the pre-change plain-string shape was also refused rather than served.

Red check: I deleted the cached field and watched the recompute line come straight back, then let it rewrite and confirmed the quiet hit returned. I then stored a body that parses but violates AntibioticResolution's precondition - the read logged Discarding an unusable cached antibiotic resolution with a ValueInstantiationException and still answered 200 with the correct drugs, so it fails open rather than taking down the alerting path. Both flips were reverted.

Automation: the existing cache tests all mock RedisService and cover the fail-open branches. I would add tests for the empty resolution being stored and reused, for a body that trips the precondition rather than the parser, for case-scoped vs user-scoped invalidation, and for the launch and scheduling paths dropping the key after commit.
